Change c0162. Location: 1818 Vol. I, Ch. VI; 1831 Ch. VII.

Context before (unchanged): We were soon joined by Elizabeth.

1818 text: Time had made great alterations in her form since I had last beheld her. Six years before she had been a pretty, good-humoured girl, whom every one loved and caressed. She was now a woman in stature and expression of countenance, which was uncommonly lovely. An open and capacious forehead gave indications of a good understanding, joined to great frankness of disposition. Her eyes were hazel, and expressive of mildness, now through recent affliction allied to sadness. Her hair was of a rich, dark auburn, her complexion fair, and her figure slight and graceful.

1831 text: Time had altered her since I last beheld her; it had endowed her with loveliness surpassing the beauty of her childish years. There was the same candour, the same vivacity, but it was allied to an expression more full of sensibility and intellect.

result.rationale: The 1818 physical description (hazel eyes, auburn hair, fair complexion, slight figure, 'great alterations in her form') is removed and replaced by a shorter, more abstract account of loveliness, candour, and sensibility; the replacement is not a like-for-like substitution of detail.
